The application of equation 6.9 and subsequent expansion in terms of differential operators acting on seed functions can be carried out for arbitrary trees.

## 7 Conclusions and outlook

In this work, we have provided a differential representation of tree-level wavefunction coefficients for massless scalars and gravitons in de Sitter. Our representation is valid for general boost breaking interactions satisfying the bound in (2.1). In Section 6 we have shown how to generalise this representation to cover also gravitational interactions in GR with minimal coupling, which violate (2.1). The differential representation involves purely algebraic operations and so side-steps the need to calculate the nested time integrals that arise in the usual bulk representation based on Feyman-Witten rules. We have provided a series of concrete examples to show how the differential representation is computationally less laborious than the time-integral representation, especially for diagrams with two or more internal propagators. Also, the final result in terms of differential operators takes a relative compact form. On the one hand, this form can already be used for algebraic manipulations. On the other hand, it can be expanded into a fully explicit rational function in a fraction of a second using computer software such as Mathematica. Finally, the differential representation has the property to completely eliminate time from the calculation, which might make it more attune to a potential holographic description of perturbative QFT in de Sitter.

This research can be extended as follows:

- • It would be interesting to understand how bulk locality constrains the form of the differential operator that acts on the flat spacetime seed $\psi^{\text{flat}}$ to give the dS wavefunction. This might have some relation to the recently discussed manifestly local test [18].

- • One should be able to build a minor modification of our construction that computes the wavefunction for boost-breaking interactions of a conformally coupled scalar. Related to this, it would be nice to understand the connection of our procedure to the formalism of the cosmological polytopes of [3, 5, 11].

## Appendix A Derivation of Propagator Relations

Here we derive the propagator relations upon which our analysis rests. Consider the massless propagator in de Sitter and flat space respectively,

$$ \displaystyle G(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k) \displaystyle=\frac{i}{2k^{3}}\left[\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta)\phi_{k}(\eta^{\prime})\theta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})+\phi_{k}(\eta)\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta^{\prime})\theta(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)-\phi_{k}(\eta)\phi_{k}(\eta^{\prime})\right]\,,\vskip 14.22636pt \displaystyle G_{\text{flat}}(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k) \displaystyle=\frac{i}{2k}\left[e^{-ik(\eta-\eta^{\prime})}\theta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})+e^{-ik(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)}\theta(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)-e^{ik(\eta+\eta^{\prime})}\right]\,, $$

where the de Sitter propagator is composed of the massless mode functions

$$ \phi_{k}(\eta)=(1-ik)e^{ik\eta}\,. $$

Now consider the two time-derivative propagator $G_{\phi^{\prime}\phi^{\prime}}=\partial_{\eta}\partial_{\eta^{\prime}}G$ integrated against some function $F(\eta,\eta^{\prime})$

$$ \int\limits_{-\infty}^{0}d\eta d\eta^{\prime}F(\eta,\eta^{\prime})\partial_{\eta}\partial_{\eta^{\prime}}G(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)\,. $$

When the time derivatives hit both mode functions one gets $k^{2}\eta\eta^{\prime}G_{\text{flat}}(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)$ . Now we turn to the terms hitting the $\theta$ -functions. First we consider terms where a single $\theta$ -function is hit. This contributes

$$ \frac{2i\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})}{2k}\left[\phi^{\star}_{k}(\eta)\partial_{\eta^{\prime}}\phi_{k}(\eta^{\prime})-\phi_{k}(\eta)\partial_{\eta^{\prime}}\phi^{\star}_{k}(\eta^{\prime})\right]=-2\eta\eta^{\prime}\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})\,. $$

Finally, we consider when both $\theta$ -functions are hit with the derivative, which gives

$$ \int d\eta d\eta^{\prime}F(\eta,\eta^{\prime})\frac{i}{2k^{3}}\left[\phi_{k}(\eta)\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta^{\prime})\partial_{\eta}\delta(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)-\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta)\phi_{k}(\eta^{\prime})\partial_{\eta}\delta(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)\right]\,. $$

We now integrate by parts in $\eta$ . The non-vanishing contribution comes from the derivative hitting the mode functions. This gives us

$$ \displaystyle\int d\eta d\eta^{\prime}F(\eta,\eta^{\prime})\frac{i}{2k^{3}}\left[\phi_{k}(\eta^{\prime})\partial_{\eta}\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta)-\phi_{k}^{\star}(\eta^{\prime})\partial_{\eta}\phi_{k}(\eta)\right]\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})=\int d\eta d\eta^{\prime}F(\eta,\eta^{\prime})[\eta\eta^{\prime}\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})]\,. $$

Summing the contributions we recover (2.10),

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{\eta}\partial_{\eta^{\prime}}G(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)=\eta\eta^{\prime}\left[k^{2}G_{\text{flat}}(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)-\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})\right]\,. $$

Now we consider generating the $\phi\phi$ and mixed $\phi^{\prime}\phi$ de Sitter propagators from the flat space propagator. First note that the mixed propagator $G_{\phi^{\prime}\phi}$ is

$$ \displaystyle\partial_{\eta}G(\eta,\eta^{\prime})=\frac{i}{2k}\left[\eta(1-ik\eta^{\prime})e^{-ik(\eta-\eta^{\prime})}\theta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})+\eta(1+ik\eta^{\prime})e^{-ik(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)}\theta(\eta^{\prime}-\eta)-\eta(1-ik\eta^{\prime})e^{ik(\eta+\eta^{\prime})}\right]\,. $$

Notice that the single-derivative hitting the $\theta$ -function vanishes on the support of the $\delta$ -function it generates. Given the mode function relation

$$ \displaystyle(1-\eta\partial_{\eta})e^{ik\eta}=(1-ik\eta)e^{ik\eta}\,, $$

we have

$$ \displaystyle G_{\phi^{\prime}\phi} \displaystyle=\partial_{\eta}G(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)=(1-\eta^{\prime}\partial_{\eta^{\prime}})G_{\text{flat}}(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)\,, \displaystyle G(\eta,\eta^{\prime}) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{k^{2}}\left[(1-\eta\partial_{\eta})(1-\eta^{\prime}\partial_{\eta^{\prime}})G_{\text{flat}}(\eta,\eta^{\prime},k)+\eta\eta^{\prime}\delta(\eta-\eta^{\prime})\right]\,, $$

where the $\delta$ -function in the above expression for $G$ comes from analogous integration by parts manipulations on the term with two derivatives.
